question: Apply CCA to find linear relationships between two sets of variables. Compute the maximum number of canonical components (min of the number of variables in each set). Report the canonical correlations.

files.eval_guideline: Canonical correlation values per component must match the reference within +/-1e-3; column order and label naming may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The filenames match exactly, and both paths indicate CSV format. The candidate directly corresponds to the requested canonical correlations from CCA of dataset_X.csv and dataset_Y.csv.

parameters.question: Compare canonical correlations component by component, requiring all min(number of X variables, number of Y variables) canonical components. Values must match within an absolute tolerance of 0.001; column order and label naming may differ.

files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires component-level numeric agreement within ±0.001 while allowing column order and label differences. Approximate comparison supports this alignment and value-by-value evaluation of the canonical correlations.

align_plan.reasoning: Both tables represent canonical components as rows, so no transpose is needed. Map the two reference columns directly and exclude the candidate's additional statistics. Physical row order is immaterial when component identities are preserved. All eight canonical correlations match within the required tolerance of 0.001.
